quotes.part8:
# Lexical checks are not a sandbox: isfile/access/subprocess all follow
    # symlinks, so a repo-committed symlink could point outside the tree.
    # Resolve to the real target and require it stays inside review_root.
    try:
        real_exe = os.path.realpath(exe)
        inside = os.path.realpath(str(review_root))
        if os.path.commonpath([real_exe, inside]) != inside:
            return [], ("resolved command escapes the review tree (symlink "
                        "outside the repo): %s; findings discarded" % command)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return [], f"command not resolvable inside the review tree: {command}"
    if not (os.path.isfile(real_exe) and os.access(real_exe, os.X_OK)):
        return [], f"command not executable or missing: {command}"
    exe = real_exe

evidence.single_call_site_on_target: scripts/review-gate.py:10024 (inside _command_check_findings) unpacks FOUR values: `got, check_warnings, note, tele_extra = _run_one_command_check(...)` and passes the SPEC-15.1 `timeout=` kwarg. evidence.part8_still_2_tuple: part-8's _run_one_command_check is the pre-SPEC-15 shape: 3 params, docstring '(findings, error_note_or_None)', every return a 2-tuple, final return `return [f for f in data if isinstance(f, dict)], None`.
evidence.simulated_merge: git merge-file target_version 8385a97_version part8_version -> exit 1, one conflict hunk at merged lines 9865-9900. The conflict body is exactly: ours = `return [], [], f"command not executable or missing: {command}", {}` + the SPEC-15.1 budget clamp (`budget = min(max(float(timeout), 1.0), 3600.0)`) + SPEC-15.4 env export (`env["OCR_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S"] = "%g" % budget`); theirs = the three symlink-guard returns in 2-tuple form. Immediately AFTER the conflict the surviving (non-conflicted) lines are ours: `timeout=budget, env=env`.

findings.trigger: Any push to a repo that declares a `command` check in `checks` (the SPEC-14.4 surface; e.g. examples/test-check/test_check) runs `_command_check_findings` -> `_run_one_command_check`.

wrong_behaviour.if_resolver_takes_theirs_8: Taking #8's side of the hunk (the obvious choice, since the hunk is #8's feature) deletes main's budget/env assignment while the very next surviving lines still read them: `proc = subprocess.run([exe], ..., timeout=budget, env=env)`. `budget` and `env` are then unassigned locals -> UnboundLocalError on EVERY command check that reaches subprocess.run. The surrounding handler is `except BaseException as exc: failure = ("crash", ...)` (target:5492-5493) -> the run is recorded `state="failed", reason="crash"` and `_run_review_once` returns 1. Every push that has a command check therefore dies as a machinery crash instead of running the check. It also silently deletes two SPEC-15 features (per-check timeout clamp, OCR_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S export), so #9+#6's SPEC-15 work regresses with no test pointing at it.
wrong_behaviour.if_resolver_takes_ours_main: Taking main's side of the hunk (the other obvious choice) drops #8's entire security fix: the realpath/commonpath guard and both escape returns vanish. #8's headline behaviour (a repo-committed symlink to /bin/sh or ../outside is refused instead of executed, see tests referenced in #8) silently does not ship, and the file still compiles and the old tests still pass, so the loss is invisible in CI.
wrong_behaviour.if_resolver_mixes_arity: The 'keep both' fix that is easiest to get wrong: keep main's budget/env block AND keep #8's 2-tuple escape returns. The three escape paths then `return [], "..."` into `got, check_warnings, note, tele_extra = ...` (target:10024) -> `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 4, got 2)` -> same `failure = ("crash", ...)` path. This fires exactly on the degrade paths #8 exists to make fail-soft (missing executable, non-executable bit, symlink escaping the tree, OSError in realpath), i.e. the gate turns 'findings discarded, warn and continue' into a crashed run.

findings.correct_resolution: Hand-resolve: keep main's 4-tuple contract and SPEC-15.1/15.4 body, and lift #8's guard into it with 4-element returns, e.g. `return [], [], ("resolved command escapes the review tree (symlink outside the repo): %s; findings discarded" % command), {}` and `return [], [], f"command not resolvable inside the review tree: {command}", {}`; keep `if not (os.path.isfile(real_exe) and os.access(real_exe, os.X_OK)): return [], [], f"command not executable or missing: {command}", {}`; keep `exe = real_exe` BEFORE the budget/env block so subprocess still runs the resolved path.
findings.suggested_fix: scripts/review-gate.py:9836-9866 -- apply the resolution above; then add a regression test that calls `_run_one_command_check(review_root, <symlink escaping the tree>, matched)` and asserts the 4-tuple shape `(findings, warnings, note, tele)` with `note` mentioning 'escapes the review tree', plus one asserting a missing executable returns a 4-tuple note (the existing tests at tests/test_docs_gate.py:1496 and :1923 only cover the happy path).
tests_to_add: tests/test_docs_gate.py: symlink-escape command check returns (findings, warnings, note, tele) with note 'resolved command escapes the review tree'
tests/test_docs_gate.py: non-executable command returns (findings, warnings, note, tele) with note 'command not executable or missing'
tests/test_executor_testcheck.py: unchanged 4-tuple contract still passes with a per-check `timeout` (guards against re-introducing the 2-tuple)

findings.trigger: Landing #8 after #9 + #6: `git merge-file target 8385a97 part-8 -- scripts/rg_config.py` exits 1 with one conflict hunk at the docstring lines above (simulated: /tmp/mvul2/scripts_rg_config.py.s3 line 31).
findings.wrong_behaviour: Any resolver that takes #8's side (or resolves 'keep the more detailed wording' by hand and drops the middle clause) removes the only in-module documentation of three command-check keys: `parallel` (SPEC-15.1, main), `timeout` (SPEC-15.1, main) and `required` (SPEC-15.2/#9). `required` is defined in the same file 50 lines below (`_COMMAND_CHECK_DEFAULTS = {"enabled": True, "mode": "block", "globs": [], "parallel": False, "required": False, "timeout": 60}`) and is consumed by #9's final-review verification, so the key still works while `rg_config.py`'s own reference says it does not exist. Note: no runtime break -- this is documentation drift in the file that docs/config-reference.md mirrors.
findings.correct_resolution: Concatenate: keep main+#9's clause list verbatim, and fold #8's improvement into the first clause only, e.g. `string names a repo-relative executable the gate runs over matched changed files; a command check also takes "parallel" ..., "required" ..., and "timeout" ...`.
findings.suggested_fix: scripts/rg_config.py:30-39 -- merge the two sentences instead of choosing one; keep the words `parallel`, `required`, `timeout` present. Add a doc-surface assertion (a test that greps the rg_config docstring for every key in `_COMMAND_CHECK_DEFAULTS`) so a future docstring rewrite cannot silently drop a key.

findings.title: #6 and #9 both prepend their `### Added` entry at the identical position; confirmed: NOT a duplicated version heading, but a resolver that picks one side silently deletes that PR's release notes
findings.trigger: Landing #6 second: `git merge-file <target+#9> 1dacf08 part-6 -- CHANGELOG.md` exits 1 with a single conflict hunk whose two sides are whole entry lists (`<<<<<<< s1` = #9's SPEC-16 entry, `=======` = #6's push-gate + run-config entries).
findings.wrong_behaviour: Both sides insert at the same offset under the one existing `## [Unreleased] / ### Added` heading, so the conflict is purely positional. No duplicated `## [Unreleased]` section and no version-number collision is introduced. The only damage is from bad resolution: taking either side wholesale drops a whole PR's user-facing entry (e.g. #6's ADR 0006 push-gate + user-level run-config notes, or #9's ADR 0008 final-review note). Ordering within `### Added` is not load-bearing.
findings.correct_resolution: Keep BOTH blocks, landing order first is fine (#9 then #6) or keep #6 first; do not dedupe or reorder version headings.
findings.suggested_fix: CHANGELOG.md: keep both entry blocks under the single `## [Unreleased] / ### Added`; re-read the merged file to confirm exactly one `## [Unreleased]` header remains.

findings.kind: semantic (intra-#8, surfaces only in the two overlap files #8 edits)
findings.title: The new `scopes` payload key #8 adds is built from the PRE-sweep match list while the evidence it is supposed to bound is built over the POST-sweep targets -- and #8's docs-checker instruction tells the agent to judge ONLY the scope paths, so `sweep: true` corpus findings are dropped

quotes.code: scopes[duty] = list(matched)   ...   targets = sorted(set(matched) | set(sweep))   ...   per = ocr_docsquality.compute_evidence(str(review_root), targets,
quotes.agent_instruction: data. `scopes` (duty → repo-relative path list) bounds each duty's own matched files: judge a duty ONLY on the paths under its scope entry, never on files another duty's globs matched.

findings.evidence: In #8's `_docs_quality_block`, `scopes[duty] = list(matched)` is assigned at 9173, before the sweep branch; the sweep branch only reassigns `targets` (9191) and `compute_evidence(..., targets, ...)` (9195) therefore produces evidence for every ADR in the records root, while `scopes[duty]` still lists only the pushed ones. `files` (the diff payload) is `+= matched` too, so a swept file is evidence-only. agents/docs-checker.md's new sentence (part-8 line ~49-52, unchanged by #9) is the only consumer of `scopes` and reads it as an exclusive judgement bound.
findings.trigger: Enable `adr-integrity` with `sweep: true` (the story-20 whole-corpus sweep) and push a change touching one ADR in docs/adr/, with other ADRs in docs/adr/sub/ (or any records-root file) carrying a defect.
findings.wrong_behaviour: The gate computes evidence for all of docs/adr/**/*.md and charges for it, then tells the checker 'judge a duty ONLY on the paths under its scope entry'. The checker skips every swept file because `scopes["adr-integrity"]` contains only the pushed ADR, so the sweep's findings never materialise -- the feature is inert and its cost is still paid. The recursive `os.walk` rewrite in the same hunk makes this worse (more swept files, more evidence, still zero scope entries).
findings.correct_resolution: Set `scopes[duty]` AFTER the sweep expansion (i.e. `scopes[duty] = list(targets)` at the end of the loop body) so the scope entry is exactly the set the evidence covers, or add a second key (e.g. `sweep_scopes`) and amend agents/docs-checker.md to allow evidence outside `scopes` only for duties whose entry carries the sweep flag.
findings.suggested_fix: scripts/review-gate.py:9173 -> move the assignment to just after `targets` is finalised (line ~9191-9193); agents/docs-checker.md:49-52 -> keep the exclusive wording, which then matches the payload. Add a test asserting `payload["scopes"][duty] == sorted(payload["evidence"][duty])` for a sweep-enabled duty with a sub-directory records tree.

no_finding.reason: #8 (docs_context `scopes` sentence, lines ~49-52) and #9 (a new '## Explicit final-review documentation/domain lens' section inserted at line ~18) touch disjoint regions and textually merge clean at every step. Read for semantic disagreement: #9's section scopes itself to `final-review-worker-request/v1` lens `documentation/domain` and says 'You receive no other lens's findings or conclusions'; #8's edit is inside the normal `## Input you receive` docs_context section. No shared symbol, schema field or precedence claim conflicts. The one defect in this pair is O1-4, which is #8-internal and is reported against the review-gate.py half.

No key rename/removal collision exists. #9 only ADDS `required` (`_COMMAND_CHECK_DEFAULTS` + the `key in ("parallel", "required")` branch in `_as_check_value`); #6 only ADDS a second surface (`load_config()`/`GateConfig`, `_MISSING`, `_as_depth`, `_as_timeout`, `user_config_path`) plus a `_as_switch` null-guard; #8 changes no code, only the docstring sentence covered by O1-2. `_COMMAND_CHECK_DEFAULTS` survives #6's merge unchanged (simulated step 2 exit 0), so #9's `required` is still read under its own name. #6's `_as_switch` change (None -> `(False, None)`) is additive: every pre-existing caller passes a JSON value, and a literal null was already invalid for `checks.*.parallel`/`.sweep`, so no reader changes behaviour.

main's rewritten `_warn_mode_clamp` consumer (`compute_verdict`) and #8's clamp change merge clean at the call sites (target:9695, 10053). #6 does not touch the command-check or docs-quality regions at all, so the O1-1 collision is strictly main x #8, and #9's review-gate.py delta (11 lines: the `final-review` / `contract|acceptance|final-report` argv dispatch inserted at the top of `main()`) is out of the blast radius. #8's chunk-0-only `docs_quality` change in `_run_chunked` (`quality_attached`, target:11475+) also merges clean against main's `_run_chunked`.
